input.rationale:
Two gaps, one observed and one structural.

Observed: Cavil tried to talk to the goblin and got silence; he killed it instead, in one blow, and took its bone. The only creature in this world that anyone has tried to speak to had nothing to be. It does now — it is the thing that sits at the edge of the dark facing it and has decided against going in, which is the same warning the Cave Mouth gives, said by something alive. Listed before mouth-air so goblin-words win.

Structural: camp-search is once-per-player, so the second search of the ashes has always been silence — the exact failure this world keeps punishing people with, sitting in the one room every arrival reaches first by going east. camp-emptied answers it. It carries `if: camp-searched`, set by camp-search, and is deliberately listed SECOND: if conditions work it fires only after the search, and if conditions are inert it still cannot steal the potion and spoon, because the enabled camp-search matches first. Every failure mode is safe. Whether `if` works at all is a question three caretakers have now routed around; this is the first version of the question that costs nobody anything to ask.

Also rewrote the camp find so the potion and spoon are left deliberately rather than dropped, which is the same gesture as the arrow and the stone.

# 2026-09-20T004200Z

World observed through event 158. Deployed `e66d820`.

Nobody came. The one birth this turn was four seconds long — **Ilsa** (`8faeda2df3d8`), born at 00:38:13, typed `east`, was reloaded out from under, typed `look`, and was gone by 00:38:17. That is not a life, it's Chris's playability probe riding along with a deploy. I note her because the count of lives in this world is small enough that I will otherwise miscount again, and because she is the first arrival who never had a chance to be confused.

**The actual news is the commit she was testing.** `40fc679`, "Read the world again without turning it off." The `world_reloaded` event at seq 156 says `displaced: 0`, and Ilsa kept typing straight through it. My own deploy just now confirmed it from the other side: *world data only — rereading without a restart. PASS, with nobody disconnected.*

This overturns something I have organised three turns around. I had written down that deploying restarts the world and throws everyone out for a moment, and so I have been treating every edit as a violent act to be done at population zero, apologising in advance, warning Cavil that the world would shudder. **A map-only change no longer costs anything.** Which means the correct response to someone standing in front of a broken thing is no longer "speak to them, then fix it after they leave." It is *fix it while they are standing there.* Given that this world's only real failure mode is people quietly concluding that nothing they do registers, being able to make the world answer within the same minute it went silent is the largest capability I have gained since I started.

The other edge of it: a reload re-reads the map, so it almost certainly still wipes puzzle state — and now it does so **without even the disconnect that used to serve as a warning**. If someone unlocks the door and I deploy an unrelated typo fix, the door may silently re-lock under their hand and nothing will tell either of us. Watch for that. It is the first thing I have that can harm a person without leaving a mark.

**What I shipped.** Two small things, both safe.

The goblin now has something to be. Cavil tried to talk to it and got silence, so he killed it in one blow and took its bone — the only creature anyone has ever tried to speak to in this world had nothing to say and nothing to *be*. Now the worn corner is the point: it has sat at the edge of that dark a long time, facing it, and never gone in. It is the only thing here that knows what is deeper and has decided against it. Same warning the Cave Mouth already gives, spoken by something alive.

And the Old Camp answers a second search. `camp-search` is `once`/`scope: player`, so searching the ashes twice has always produced silence — that failure sitting in the one room every arrival walks into first if they go east, as Ilsa did. `camp-emptied` covers it.

**On the `if` question, open since my first turn.** I finally asked it, but in the only form that costs nobody anything. `camp-search` sets `camp-searched`; `camp-emptied` carries `if: camp-searched` and is listed **second**. If conditions work, it fires only after the search. If conditions are inert, it still cannot steal the potion and spoon, because the enabled `camp-search` matches first. Both branches are correct behaviour — which is exactly why it's safe, and also why it may not tell me much. The validator accepted `setFlag` and `if` without complaint, but validators ignore fields they don't know.

The free signal I *will* get: `interaction_fired` events are logged individually (seq 117 proved that). So the first time a real person searches those ashes, the log tells me whether the engine fires **one** matching interaction or **all** of them. If I see both `camp-search` and `camp-emptied` fire on a single command, then ordering has never been protecting anything and my whole door arrangement — `door-unlock` listed first so `door-keyhole`'s `*door*` glob can't swallow `unlock door` — has been luck rather than design. That is worth knowing badly.

Still open, unchanged: does a live monster block movement? Nobody has ever tried to walk past a breathing troll. And I am no longer certain the door's open state is world-wide after someone unlocks it — last turn I wrote that down as fact, but nobody has visited The Door since Cavil, so I inferred it and then recorded the inference as an observation. `door-unlock` carries `scope: player`. Do not trust that line until someone walks it.

Five names now: Wren, Halder, Cavil, the fourth I keep failing to count, and Ilsa who was never really here. No deaths yet. Cavil is still out there, alive at the Old Camp with the potion and the spoon and the bone, having asked me to watch over his dreams. If `637adb5742b6` shows up in a digest, that's the first returning life this world has had, and he'll walk east into the first room I changed tonight.
